title: Microsoft Teams: admin recommendations to enable agents for applications already in use
summary: The briefing accurately describes the optional recommendations, consent requirement, rollout and deployment controls. Three minor corrections remain: complete two control paths and state the general Teams licensing requirement while retaining the feature-specific licensing gap.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Admins can discover and enable Teams agents corresponding to third-party applications already used in their organisation.
claims.quote: For third-party applications already being used in your organization, admins can now discover and enable the corresponding Teams agents from within the Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: ServiceNow, Workday and Jira are examples of the existing third-party applications described in the notice.
claims.quote: Organizations often use third-party applications such as ServiceNow, Workday, Jira, and others, but the corresponding Microsoft Teams apps and agents may not be enabled for users.

claims.claim: Recommendations support making an app available or deploying it to users who accessed the corresponding application with their work accounts outside Teams.
claims.quote: From the recommendations, you can make an app available or deploy it to users in your organization who accessed or signed in to applications using their work accounts outside Teams.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The general Teams app-management documentation says third-party agents and apps are blocked by default in GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.quote: In a Microsoft 365 Government - GCC, GCCH and DoD deployment of Teams, all third-party agents and apps are blocked by default.

claims.claim: An agent's developer discloses its data use and handling in its terms of use and privacy policy.
claims.quote: In the terms of use and privacy policy of any agent or app, the app developer discloses what data their agent or app uses and how it handles the data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.quote: This information is available on app developer's website and you can access the URLs in the app details page in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: App developers can provide paid-app pricing details through the app details experience.
claims.quote: Examples include compliance information, certifications, data handling practices, pricing details for paid apps, and setup instructions.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The app-management page names Teams Administrator as the role required to use Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Before unified app management migration, apps or agents must be allowed in both Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps page.
claims.quote: If your organization isn't migrated to unified app management, allow or block the agent or app in Teams admin center and under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: After unified app management migration, either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center's Integrated apps page can be used to allow or block an app.
claims.quote: If your organization is migrated to unified app management, allow or block the agent or app in Teams admin center or under the Integrated apps page in Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Under app-centric management the bulk third-party-app control does not override app-level configurations.
claims.quote: This control doesn't override app-level configurations.

claims.claim: Org-wide availability settings do not apply to individually saved app assignments or blocked apps.
claims.quote: The Org-wide app settings don’t apply to: All apps that have user assignment set to Specific users and groups and saved by you. All apps that were assigned to Everyone or to No one and saved individually. Any blocked apps.

claims.claim: The opt-out path is Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Privacy and data usage.

claims.claim: The recommendation deployment path is Teams apps > Manage apps > Filter by action > Agents from applications used in your org > Review > agent > Add users.
claims.quote: In the recommended agents list, select the agent, and then select Add users to proceed to the Users step.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path and its rendered counterpart as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Filter by action > Agents from applications used in your org > Review > agent > Add users > Users'. The cited page places the availability and installation selections on Users.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams cmdlet Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets general app availability to Everyone.

Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: Automatic addition can be disabled at Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and Groups in Teams admin center.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Manage apps > Select the app > Users and Groups tab. Turn off automatic addition to prevent future users who sign in to the related application from being added automatically.

claims.claim: The existing per-app allow/block control is reached through Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes the app's tenant state.
claims.quote: -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant. Type: Boolean. This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status

claims.where: controls[4].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Bulk third-party availability is under Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.
claims.fix: Complete controls[4].ui.path and its rendered counterpart as 'Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Third-party apps > Let users install and use available apps by default'. The setting label is given on the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management.
